title: Queues, skills, and wrap-up
summary: Queue media settings, skills, wrap-up codes, callbacks, and service level.

lessons.title: Create the queue in a division
lessons.summary: The queue is a named waiting line in one division, with at most 5,000 members.
paras: Menu path in the article is User Management, then Queues. You set a unique name without special characters, an optional peer id for an external platform, the division, and an optional default language. You can copy settings and members from an existing queue and edit after.

Copying a queue copies its routing method too. If the source uses predictive routing or a five-ring bullseye, the copy is not a blank standard queue. Read the routing tab after the copy. The new queue still needs its own in-queue flow assignment if you do not want the org default.

lessons.title: Skills and proficiency are on the agent
lessons.summary: The queue asks for skills. The agent profile holds them. Evaluation decides whether proficiency matters.
paras: ACD skills are tags with a proficiency. All-skills matching ignores the number and demands the tag. Best available skills uses the average proficiency inside the 100 longest-idle window. A skill the interaction does not require does not help or hurt that interaction.

Bullseye can express the same skill at a lower proficiency on an outer ring by using groups, which the overview prefers when WEM forecasts must stay stable. Removing the skill entirely is the other style. Agents inactive for the 7 day window described in the evaluation article are not candidates even if their profile looks perfect.

lessons.title: After call work and the system wrap-up codes
lessons.summary: ACW is optional, discretionary, or time-boxed. The platform has its own codes when agents do not finish.
paras: Optional ACW lets the agent skip wrap-up. Mandatory discretionary lets them end ACW themselves. Mandatory time-boxed caps the duration. If Optional or Mandatory discretionary is on, the interaction stays open until the agent ends it. If they log off or close the browser during ACW, it stays open unless you enable End Interactions Automatically when Agents Logoff, which closes it with ININ-SYSTEM-LOGOUT.

If the timer expires before a required code is chosen, Genesys Cloud assigns ININ-WRAP-UP-TIMEOUT. Callbacks require a wrap-up code even when ACW is Optional. Agents can save codes and notes only if they actually enter ACW. A direct transfer can still force a code from the previous queue’s list. Outbound dialing has its own codes. The article says not to use the agent-requested option on outbound campaigns because agents can skip the work the campaign needs.

lessons.title: Wrap-up codes live in divisions too
lessons.summary: The codes an agent sees are the codes their role can see, and Genesys wants them in the queue’s division.
paras: The queue article says you add wrap-up codes that your role can see, and it recommends codes assigned to the same division as the queue so reports make sense. A code in another division is a reporting split even if an admin with broad access managed to attach it.

Internal calls made on behalf of a queue can hand the receiving agent that queue’s ACW settings and codes. The article’s escape is to place a direct internal call instead of calling on behalf of the queue. The receiving agent may still see the interaction as ACD. Read that note before you debug “wrong code list” on an internal consult.

lessons.title: Service level is a percentage and a target in seconds
lessons.summary: Each media has a service level percentage and a target duration. That pair is what conditional routing and WFM both mean by “the goal.”
paras: The queue article tells you to set a service level percentage and a service level target in seconds per channel. Voice, chat, email, message, and callback are configured on their own media panels. A single number for “the queue” is not how the admin page works. A voice target of 20 seconds and an email target of an hour can both be honest.

Conditional group routing’s KPI is only meaningful if this pair exists and you believe it. WEM service goal templates, covered in the WFM track, are the planning version of the same idea. Do not set the queue target to 1 second to “look good.” The percentage will tell on you.

lessons.title: Callbacks are interactions with their own rules
lessons.summary: A callback is queued work. It still needs a wrap-up code, and it counts as its own utilization slot.
paras: CX 1 includes callbacks. The utilization default is one callback, and preview calls are treated as callbacks. Calls and callbacks do not interrupt each other by default, so an agent on a live call is not also offered a callback. The queue’s callback media panel has its own service level.

The wrap-up article says a callback requires a wrap-up code even if voice ACW is Optional. Preferred-agent behavior also notes that for email, messaging, and inbound callbacks the platform no longer routes to the last handling agent, while scheduled callbacks are a different case. Read that sentence on the preferred-agent page before you promise “the same agent will call back.”
lessons.uncertainty: Scheduled callbacks are called out separately from inbound callbacks on the preferred-agent page. Confirm the current sentence before you design a scheduled campaign around last-agent behavior.

lessons.title: Membership, On Queue, and the copy trap
lessons.summary: A copied queue can duplicate a bullseye you did not mean to clone.
paras: Membership is the list of agents who may receive the queue’s work, up to 5,000. On Queue is the status that actually enters them. Copying settings and members is a shortcut and a trap: routing method, evaluation, bullseye rings, wrap-up, and ACW come along. The article says you can edit after the copy. Do that before the queue takes a DID.

An agent in the member list who is off queue, fully utilized, or missing a required skill under all-skills matching will not be offered the interaction. The simulator makes those three filters obvious. Production adds the 7 day activity window and the scoring across queues.

fault.title: Inherited rings
fault.symptom: A new overflow queue waits 72 hours on ring 1 because the source was a specialty queue.

fault.fix: Set a delay that matches this queue’s promise, publish nothing else until a test call expands the way you expect.
